title: The release-tier CI is green on Windows: prove-gates' pool lifecycle and the sweep's deadline replay
desiredOutcome: Release-tier CI (ci.yml -f tier=release) green on the commit carrying P142, P144 and these fixes, every windows selftests shard included

findings.issue: pw5's registration conjunct `(still == [respelled] or (respelled is None and os.name == "nt"))` drops the second-spelling check entirely when os.symlink fails on Windows (no privilege). On that platform pw5 then proves only the reaper's old forward-slash behaviour, so the Windows-only half of the fix (canonical comparison of a differently spelled tree) is covered by pw14's injected resolver alone and never by a real git listing. The default `_canonical_path` (realpath + normcase on a real nt) is likewise not exercised against a real 8.3 name by any case this task adds; the only evidence that realpath expands RUNNER~1 is the pw6 line in CI log 123039432291.log, read on the runner's Python.
findings.resolution: No code change needed for the product. Either make pw5 fail loudly (not silently narrow) when the link cannot be made on nt, or note in the case text which spelling was exercised; confirm on the next windows-latest run that pw5, pw6 and pw13 pass with the symlink branch actually taken.

review.outcome: [findings: 1 - 0 high, 0 med, 1 low; 0 with a recorded fix commit]

tasks.title: The sweep's deadline-replay case tt3c holds on a slow windows runner
tasks.description: Release-tier CI run 40751590388 (f10ed750), windows cp1252 2: tools/sweep-selftests.py --selftest fails tt3c only (152/153); every other leg passes it. Log: <scratchpad>/ci144/123039432306.log (gh run view 40751590388 --job 123039432306 --log-failed). The case: a staged suite cut by the deadline is still replayed past it, its timed-out block and its refused block each one failing case naming why. Observed: ok False after 2.7s with x-block 'did not finish within 2s' and y-block 'not started: the sweep's deadline of 2s had passed', 0/2 cases. Read what tt3c asserts and decide whether the PRODUCT is wrong under a slow windows runner (e.g. the replay itself bounded by the expired deadline, or a race between the kill and the replay) or the case depends on wall-clock margins a loaded windows runner cannot hold (a 2 s deadline with process start-up of about a second on windows). Fix the product where it is wrong; where the case's timing is the fault, make the case's verdict independent of runner speed (inject the clock or the timeout) rather than widen a number. Show it red-first by reproducing the slow-runner timing on POSIX (inject a start-up delay).

outcome.technical: Diagnosis: the product was right and the case depended on runner speed. On windows cp1252 2 the x-block was killed by the 2s deadline before python start-up, the _harness import (with a cold per-run pycache) and staged_main dispatch had reached its print. So the partial line was legitimately empty. The rest worked: the replay ran past the deadline, x was named as timed out, y as refused, 0/2. A product fault would have failed every windows leg, but only one failed. Fix, in the tt3c case of tools/sweep-selftests.py only (no product function changed): (1) the split-hang fixture is built by tt_hang(delay). It sleeps delay, prints the partial line, then creates a witness file (tt_box/tt-printed, outside the child's watched scratch and home) and hangs. split-quick is built from the same template without the hang, and still holds no time.sleep, as tt3b asserts. (2) tt3c runs the suite with deadline 1, 2, 4, 8 and stops at the first run whose witness exists. Run 1 delays the print 2.0s past its 1s deadline on purpose, so every runner judges a run that printed nothing. (3) On every run it asserts that ok is False, that x is named as not finishing within Ns, that y is refused with that run's own deadline, that PASS ty1 is absent, that the output ends 0/2, and that the run took under 30s. A witnessed run must carry the partial line exactly once; a run with no witness at most once, because the print comes before the witness write. If no run is witnessed the case fails, naming every deadline tried. Evidence: (a) `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --selftest` in the task tree: ALL PASS 153/153, exit 0, runs [(1s, not printed, 1.1s), (2s, printed, 2.1s)]. (b) Task gate `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tools/sweep-selftests.py`: '1/1 files ok, 153 cases', exit 0. (c) Throwaway-copy mutations: partial dropped in block_entry gave tt3c+tt3d red (151/153, exit 1); partial duplicated gave tt3c+tt3d red (151/153); a 20s delay so no run ever prints gave tt3c red (152/153), every deadline tried listed; the slow runner (2.5s delay) gave green at the 4s deadline. (d) ruff check: All checks passed; vermin -t=3.8-: no violations; _output_lints.prose_number_claims('.') = [] and house_style_violations() = []. (e) `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__refs.py`: '1/1 files ok, 292 cases' (tail through a pipe; the sweep line is the evidence). Own-tests command could-not-run, verbatim: '[run-test-gate] no phase 'P145' in this manifest', exit 2. My tree's manifest is HEAD f10ed750, and P145 is still uncommitted in the project tree. Wall time of the suite: 30.6s before, 32.1s and 32.2s after (each measured once, same machine). Run 1 adds about 1.1s. Dependants: every listed file (.claude/skills/before-you-claim/evals/evals.json, .github/sweep-costs.json, .github/workflows/ci.yml, plugins/audit/scripts/_output.py, governance/_runner_collects.py, governance/_runner_output.py, governance/stamp-verification.py, manifest/_filed_returns.py) and every listed name (budget_line, coverage_findings, default_jobs, file_timeout) is still correct. The diff touches only fixture text and the body of tt3c inside the selftest; no function signature, CLI flag, output line, cost rule or timeout rule changed. The one effect any of them can see is the suite's own seconds in .github/sweep-costs.json, about 1s more, well inside its timeout; I did not re-record the table. Brief mismatch, for the orchestrator: the launch message described prove-gates.py pw5/pw6/pw13 (that is P145.2's brief) and said not to touch sweep-selftests.py. But it named brief-145-1.md as the authority, and that brief, the manifest's files and this submit block all make P145.1 the tt3c / tools/sweep-selftests.py task. I followed the brief, in my own tree claude-plugins-P145.1, and did not touch prove-gates.py.
outcome.descriptive: tt3c's verdict no longer depends on how fast a runner starts a process: a witness file says whether the killed block printed, and the deadline doubles until it has, so the slow windows leg that failed it now passes the same assertions.

verifiedBy: tt3c reworked: the deadline-cut staged suite runs at deadlines 1, 2, 4, 8 until a witness shows the hanging block reached its print. The first run delays the print past its deadline on purpose, every run asserts the replay, the timeout, the refusal and 0/2, and the witnessed run asserts the partial line exactly once.

redFirst.basis: regression mode, expectRedFirst false, so no helper red is owed. The helper also cannot separate this case from its fix: the case and the code it runs live in the same file (tools/sweep-selftests.py), so HEAD with the test file copied over it is the fixed tree. Instead the slow runner was reproduced by hand in a throwaway git-archive copy of HEAD (scratchpad/p1451-red), not the shared tree. A 2.5s sleep was injected before the x-block's print, and HEAD's tt3c failed with exactly the Windows output: 'ok False after 2.1s ... FAIL x-block ... (did not finish within 2s) ... FAIL y-block ... (not started: the sweep's deadline of 2s had passed) ... SELFTEST FAILED: 0/2 cases passed', with no partial line, exit 1. The same 2.5s delay on every run of the fixed case gave runs [(1s, not printed), (2s, not printed), (4s, printed)], ALL PASS 153/153, exit 0.

tasks.title: prove-gates' pool reaper compares one canonical spelling of every path on Windows and never reaps a live run's pool
tasks.description: Release-tier CI run 40751590388 (f10ed750), windows plain 1 and cp1252 1: tools/prove-gates.py --selftest fails pw5, pw6, pw13 (58/61); linux and macOS pass. Logs: <scratchpad>/ci144/123039432291.log and 123039432591.log (fetch with: gh run view 40751590388 --job 123039432291 --log-failed). pw5: 'spared [] (1 registered)' - the pool whose owner is LIVE was reaped, the exact property the reaper exists to keep (reap only on an explicit dead answer). Find out why on Windows: _locks.pid_alive's Windows probe (_pid_alive_windows) answering False for a live pid, the owner file's pid, or path spelling - the logs show three spellings of one temp root on Windows (C: then <home> with forward slashes, the same with backslashes, and <home> with its 8.3 short name RUNNER~1), and git worktree list prints forward slashes. pw6: the foreign tree after reap is listed but the case still fails - read its expectation. pw13: the by-name removal refused a pool tree as 'not under the pool root' when one side is RUNNER~1 and the other runneradmin, and dropped None. Fix the PRODUCT so every comparison of a worktree path, a pool root and an admin gitdir is made on one canonical spelling on Windows (realpath alone does not expand 8.3 names on every Python; os.path.normcase plus a long-name expansion, or comparing by os.path.samefile / file identity where the path exists). A reaper that removes a live run's pool on Windows is a med defect, not a test issue. Add POSIX-runnable cases that fail before the fix by injecting the Windows spellings (short name vs long name, slash direction, case) and, for pid liveness, an injected probe. Keep prove-gates' drive protocol byte-identical.
